content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain the difference between addition and condensation polymerisation
Describe the formation of polyesters and polyamides
Identify the monomers needed to make specific condensation polymers

are formed when monomers join together and a small molecule (usually water) is released. Unlike addition polymerisation, two different types of monomers are usually needed, and a by-product is formed.
Two different monomers usually react together
Each monomer has functional groups at both ends
A small molecule (usually H₂O) is released
Ester or amide links form in the polymer chain
[DIAGRAM: Formation of polyester showing ester links and water molecules being released]
[DIAGRAM: Formation of polyamide showing amide links and water molecules being released]
"Break" the polymer at each ester link
Add -OH to one side and -H to the other
Identify the dicarboxylic acid and diol
"Break" the polymer at each amide link
Add -OH to the CO side and -H to the NH side
Identify the dicarboxylic acid and diamine
Ester and amide links can be broken by water
This is the reverse of condensation
Explain the difference between addition and condensation polymerisation.
Only one type of monomer needed
Uses monomers with functional groups at both ends
A small molecule (e.g., water) is released
Example: diol + dicarboxylic acid → polyester + water
Draw the structure of the repeating unit of the polyester formed from:
The -OH of the diol reacts with the -COOH of the acid
Name the type of polymer and identify the functional group in the link:
It is formed from the reaction of -COOH and -NH₂
State the monomers needed to make nylon-6,6 and explain where the name comes from.
The first "6" refers to the 6 carbons in the diamine
The second "6" refers to the 6 carbons in the dicarboxylic acid
Thinking condensation polymers don't release anything
Condensation releases a small molecule (usually H₂O)
Using monomers with only one functional group
Condensation monomers need functional groups at BOTH ends
Made from diol + dicarboxylic acid, contain ester links (-COO-)
Made from diamine + dicarboxylic acid, contain amide links (-CONH-)
Two monomers, small molecule released, ester/amide links
